content.title: About
content.content: Egg white is the clear liquid surrounding the yolk of a chicken egg. Raw egg white is about 90 % water and 10 % proteins, including albumin, ovalbumin and lysozyme. It contains virtually no fat or carbohydrates and very little vitamins or minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg white is composed of roughly 90 % water.
It provides all essential amino acids, making it a complete protein source.
Raw egg white is used in cooking to create airy meringues and soufflés.
When heated, the proteins coagulate, turning the clear liquid into a white, firm mass.
Lysozyme in egg white has antibacterial properties.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Egg white supplies the body with all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat and calories
items.content: Because it contains virtually no fat, egg white is suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Contains lysozyme
items.content: Lysozyme exhibits antibacterial activity and may help support the immune system.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: The abundant protein aids muscle protein synthesis, especially beneficial for active individuals.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Egg white contains very little sodium, making it a good choice for those monitoring salt intake.

items.title: Risk of salmonella
items.content: Raw egg white can be contaminated with Salmonella bacteria; using pasteurized eggs or cooking it is recommended.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Egg white is a common allergen and can cause reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Lack of vitamins and minerals
items.content: Because it contains almost no vitamins or minerals, relying solely on egg white for nutrition is not advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw egg white is frequently used in culinary applications such as meringues, soufflés, protein shakes, and baked goods. When consuming raw, choose pasteurized eggs to reduce infection risk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep eggs refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. Separated raw egg white should be used within 2‑3 days or frozen in an airtight container for up to 3 months.
